thesis: Sacred beauty can transform experience without demonstrating a metaphysical interpretation or justifying others’ suffering.

ideas.statement: Taking an experience seriously requires examining the inference from felt meaning to benevolent order; neither reduction to mechanism nor intensity settles truth.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: The imagined world-creator tests aesthetic justification, not God’s existence; austere purity can also become status performance.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: The imagined world-creator tests aesthetic justification, not God’s existence; austere purity can also become status performance.

audit.notes: Direct active-LLM reading of all units; methodological and normative boundaries retained.
